captions: Let's break down the Dhoot Transmission I-P-O —
one of the largest issues opening next week,
at three thousand and sixty-seven crore rupees.
We'll cover what the company does, its financials,
where the money actually goes,
how it's priced against its rivals,
and how much you'd need to apply.
Quick note — this is education, not investment advice,
and not a tip to buy.
So what does Dhoot Transmission do?
It makes wiring harnesses and connectors —
think of them as the electrical nervous system of a vehicle,
carrying power and signals to every part.
It supplies these to makers of two-wheelers,
cars and commercial vehicles.
It's riding a strong theme: modern and electric vehicles use far more wiring and electronics than older ones,
so the value of components per vehicle keeps climbing.
And it sells to large vehicle makers both in India and overseas —
a diversified, sticky customer base.
Let's go deeper on the business.
Who actually buys from Dhoot?
Its biggest client is Bajaj Auto —
about thirty-two percent of revenue —
then T-V-S at twenty percent, Honda at eleven,
plus Royal Enfield and Suzuki.
Beyond wiring harnesses it also makes battery packs, sensors,
switches and E-V electronics,
from twenty-two plants across India, the U-K,
Slovakia and Thailand.
On order book —
auto-parts don't quote one; they run on long-term supply programs with these OEMs.
But the flip side is concentration: the top five customers are about seventy-two percent of revenue,
so losing one would hurt.
Now the financials — and they're solid.
Revenue for the year ended March twenty twenty-six was about four thousand five hundred and sixty-four crore,
up a strong thirty-one point three three percent.
Net profit was three hundred and ninety-seven crore,
up twelve point one four percent.
Notice profit grew slower than revenue —
a sign of some margin pressure as the company scales.
The grey market is pricing a premium near twenty-eight percent,
but that's unofficial and drifts daily.
Here's the most important part of any I-P-O —
where does your money go?
Of the three thousand and sixty-seven crore,
about fourteen hundred crore — some forty-six percent —
is a fresh issue that goes into the company.
The larger part,
about one thousand six hundred and sixty-seven crore,
is an Offer for Sale —
existing shareholders selling and pocketing that cash.
So it's a fairly even split: a little over half is a sell-down,
and the rest funds the business.
What does the fresh money fund?
A large part goes to repaying borrowings,
which cuts interest costs and strengthens the balance sheet.
The rest supports capital spending and working capital,
so the company can serve rising demand from electric and premium vehicles.
And a portion is kept for general corporate purposes.
So the fresh money both de-risks the balance sheet and funds some growth.
So how is it priced against its rivals?
At about forty-five times earnings,
Dhoot is asking LESS than the peer average of roughly fifty-seven times.
Sona B-L-W trades near seventy-five,
Uno Minda around fifty-seven,
and Motherson Sumi Wiring about forty-three.
So Dhoot sits at the cheaper end of the pack —
and it earns a higher return on equity,
above sixteen percent versus around twelve for the group.
On the numbers, it looks like the better-value,
higher-quality name — though remember,
these peer multiples move with the market every day.
So — should you subscribe?
Let's weigh it honestly.
On the strengths side — revenue is up thirty-one percent,
it's priced below the peer average,
and it earns a higher return on equity than its rivals.
On the watch-out side — over half the issue is a sell-down,
profit grew slower than revenue so margins are under pressure,
and auto demand is cyclical.
The takeaway — a cyclical business, but a cheaply-priced,
higher-quality one.
Go in understanding half your money buys out sellers.
Finally — how do you apply, and how much do you need?
As a retail investor you can bid up to two lakh rupees for a thirty-five percent quota.
If it's oversubscribed, shares are given out by lottery,
so a bigger cheque does not get you more.
H-N-Is bid above two lakh for a fifteen percent quota.
For Dhoot, one lot is seventeen shares —
about fourteen thousand eight hundred and seven rupees —
your minimum.
Track the live subscription on the N-S-E and B-S-E I-P-O pages,
Chittorgarh, Moneycontrol, or your broker app.
